in_english.long_meaning: The Arabic root of the name Mamar (مأمور) is derived from the verb 'amaara' (أَمَارَ), which means 'to entrust or make someone responsible'. In Islamic tradition, the name Mamar is associated with the qualities of trustworthiness, reliability, and obedience. In the Quran, the word 'ma'mur' (مأمور) refers to a person who is given a command or a task to perform. The name Mamar is also mentioned in the Hadith, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said: 'A trustworthy and reliable servant is the most beloved of Allah.' Muslims often choose this name for their children in the hope that they will grow up to be trustworthy, dependable, and faithful servants of Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, The Conquest of Egypt, p. 152. The name Mamar was the name of the Arab tribe that inhabited the area around modern-day El Minya, Egypt before the Arab invasion in the late 7th century.
